findings.where: Nav links "Destinations" (#destinations) and "How we rank"; the wordmark home link; footer links "Privacy", "Terms", "How we rank" and "Report content"
findings.fault: Every link except the email goes nowhere. "Destinations" points to an anchor the page does not have. The wordmark, "How we rank", "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content" all reload this same page. A visitor has no way to reach another destination, the home page, the ranking method or the legal pages.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has decided Canggu isn't right and wants to compare the next stop, and a sceptical visitor who clicks "How we rank" to check the merit claim. The product says trust rests on a published ranking method, so a dead "How we rank" link works against that.

findings.fault: This one heading is set in italic turquoise with an underline, which looks exactly like a link, but it does nothing (static in the parts map). It is also styled differently from its sibling headings "Surf" and "Good for", and it uses turquoise, a fill-only colour, as text.
findings.who_objects: A visitor taps "Vibe" expecting more about the nightlife and social scene, gets nothing, and then distrusts the page's real links. Anyone scanning sees one heading out of step with the rest, which reads as a styling mistake.

findings.where: "Good for" tag list (all 12 pills, desktop and phone)
findings.fault: These static facts are drawn as bordered, filled pills that look like filter chips you can tap. They do nothing (all static in the parts map). The house reserves the selectable-chip look for filters, and this product's core feature is search and filtering by vibe.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps "First-time surfers" or "Budget" expecting to filter hostels gets no response and may think the page is broken.

findings.fault: The pills use a rainbow of unrelated fills and clashing borders: yellow with a coral border, pink with a cyan border, purple, magenta, coral-red. None of these colours means anything, and pink, purple and magenta are not in the palette. A coral-red fill used as decoration breaks the coral-is-CTA-only rule, and the result reads as random rather than branded.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand rule is that each colour has exactly one job and coral is reserved for CTAs. Visitors also read the varied colours as categories that mean something, but they don't.

findings.where: "Coming soon" announcement block, foot of page
findings.fault: The notice sits on a saturated crimson ground that is not in the palette. It looks like an error or alert. The rules say the interior announcement sits on the ink night ground. Red is also the colour of danger and sold-out states, so a calm "listings coming soon" message looks like something has gone wrong.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor reads the red box as a warning or failure at the very moment the brand needs to sound confident. The founder would object because the announcement pattern and the colour roles are fixed in DESIGN.md.

findings.fault: The heading promises a list of the best hostels, but the page lists none: listings are not live. "Best" also implies a ranking the product has not made yet. It is also in title case, which breaks the sentence-case voice rule.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker arriving from search expecting hostels feels misled when the page ends in "listings coming soon". The founder would object because "trust is the product" and the voice rules are sentence case.

findings.fault: The section that does half the brief's job (what to look for in a hostel there) gets the weakest heading on the page: a small, letter-spaced uppercase label. Its siblings "Surf", "Vibe" and "Good for" are large headings, so this section reads as a footnote. Uppercase is also reserved for badges and filter labels.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker scanning for practical hostel advice skims past it. The key takeaway ranks below the tag list.

findings.where: All body copy: intro, Surf, Vibe, What to look for and the announcement, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The text is fully justified, which opens uneven word gaps and rivers. These are worst at phone width ("MantaHostels   is   launching   across") and in short lines like the Vibe paragraph.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader scanning mid-transit, who finds the gappy lines slower and choppier to read.

findings.where: Desktop layout: text column against the tag list and announcement block
findings.fault: The text sits in a narrow left column with the right half of the screen empty, while the tag list and the red block run the full width. Inside the red block, the text stops at the same narrow column and leaves most of the box empty. The two widths look unplanned, as if the layout broke.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor planning a trip sees a lopsided page with a half-empty coloured box, which makes it look unfinished.

findings.where: First screen / top of the destination page
findings.fault: There is no destination hero: no turquoise ground, no illustration, no loud moment. The page opens on plain text on sand. The brand names destination-page top banners as the loud zone and names sterile as the enemy, yet the only energy on the page is the tag pills.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose north star is "loud moments, calm machine". The backpacker gets no sense of place or feeling from the first screen of a Bali beach-town guide.
